\[
\rho = \frac{\text{mass of unit cell}}{\text{volume of unit cell}}
\]

\[
a^3 = \frac{2M}{\rho N_A}
\]

a^3 = \frac{2 \times 55.845}{7.86 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}} \approx 2.3597 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{cm}^3

\]

To find the doubling time of the ferret population, use the exponential growth formula \(N = N_0 e^{rt}\), where \(N\) is the population at time \(t\), \(N_0\) is the initial population, \(r\) is the intrinsic growth rate, and \(t\) is time. The doubling time occurs when \(N = 2N_0\), so set up the equation:

\[
2N_0 = N_0 e^{rt}
\]

Divide both sides by \(N_0\) (assuming \(N_0 \neq 0\)):

\[
2 = e^{rt}
\]

Take the natural logarithm of both sides:

\[
\ln(2) = rt
\]

Solve for \(t\):

\[
t = \frac{\ln(2)}{r}
\]

\[
t = \frac{0.693}{1.3} \approx 0.533 \, \text{years}
\]

\[
t \approx 0.53 \, \text{years}
\]
